prompt:

Land, New Zealand – P6,000,000
Car, Philippines – P1,200,000

Loss from claims against insolvent persons – P3,000,000
Transfer for public use – P500,000
Insured loss from earthquake – P1,200,000
How much is the net taxable estate?
rationale: Gross estate (resident citizen, taxed on worldwide properties) = House Php10,000,000 + Land, New Zealand Php6,000,000 + Car Php1,200,000 = Php17,200,000. Only the transfer for public use (Php500,000) and the standard deduction (Php5,000,000) are allowable. Net taxable estate = Php17,200,000 - Php500,000 - Php5,000,000 = Php11,700,000.

prompt: A taxpayer paid excessive tax on April 15, 2000. On December 20, 2001, she filed a written claim for refund. Her claim was denied by the BIR and she received the denial on March 16, 2002. She filed a motion for reconsideration with the BIR on March 31, 2002. On April 18, 2002, she received the final denial of the BIR. What will be the taxpayer's remedy?

File an appeal with the Court of Tax Appeals within 30 days after the receipt of the final denial
File an appeal with the Court of Tax Appeals within 15 days after the receipt of the final denial
